text: Ax's theorem (1968) states that an injective polynomial map $f: \mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}^n$ must be:
choices: a bijection onto a proper subset
explanation: Ax's theorem: an injective polynomial map $\mathbb{C}^n \to \mathbb{C}^n$ is surjective (hence bijective). The model-theoretic proof transfers the easy finite-field fact through an ultraproduct to a model of $\mathrm{ACF}_0$, then to $\mathbb{C}$ by completeness of $\mathrm{ACF}_0$. Polynomial maps need not be linear, and 'constant' or 'onto a proper subset' directly contradict surjectivity.
